# Comprehensive Communication Analysis RPi ↔ Teensy — 2026-05-10

> **Objective:** identify all issues of **efficiency**, **desynchronization**, and **fail-safe** of the serial channel between the Raspberry Pi 4B and the Teensy 4.1, and propose a prioritized plan of fixes to arrive at the RCJ 2026 World Cup with a robust and fast protocol.
>
> **Audience:** mentors and students of the IITA Salta team. Coach: Gustavo Viollaz. Assigned follow-up: Enzo (`@enzzo19`) + Benjamin (`@benjaminvillagran`).
>
> This document complements, **does not replace**, [`comunicacion-rpi-teensy.md`](comunicacion-rpi-teensy.md).

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The channel works but **is not fail-safe**: if the Pi hangs, the Teensy continues moving the robot with the last command; if the Teensy resets, the Pi does not know; a single bit flip can corrupt a field without either side noticing. There are also **clear inefficiencies** (`serialEvent5()` consumes 1 byte per loop; `reset_input_buffer()` on RPi discards valid commands) that penalize response latency and produce silent command losses.

**Tactical Recommendation:** apply 6 minimum fixes without changing the protocol (covers 80% of the risk) **before** considering a protocol v2 with length+CRC. See [§7 Migration Plan](#7-plan-de-migración-por-fases).

---

## 2. Current Architecture

```
┌──────────────────┐   UART 115200, 8-N-1   ┌──────────────────┐
│  Raspberry Pi 4B │ ─────────────────────► │   Teensy 4.1     │
│   /dev/serial0   │                        │   Serial5        │
│                  │ ◄─────────────────────  │                  │
│  pyserial 3.x    │   acks of 1 byte       │  Teensyduino     │
└──────────────────┘                        └──────────────────┘
       │                                              │
       └─ vision (YOLO+OpenCV)                        └─ motors, encoders, ToF, IMU,
          high-level decision                            servos, color sensor
```

**Frame RPi → Teensy** (8 bytes, no CRC, no length):

```
[ 0xFF, speed,  0xFE, angle, 0xFD, green_state, 0xFC, silver_line ]
```

**Messages Teensy → RPi** (1 byte each, no frame):

| Byte | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0xF9` (249) | End of startUp → switch to `line` |
| `0xF8` (248) | Enough balls → switch to `deposit` |
| `0xFF` (255) | Switch off → return to `waiting` |

## 4. Efficiency Issues

### 4.1 [P1] `serialEvent5()` consumes only 1 byte per call

**File:** [`software/teensy/firmware/src/main.cpp:383-406`](../../software/teensy/firmware/src/main.cpp#L383-L406)

```cpp
void serialEvent5() {
    if (Serial5.available() > 0) {
        int data = Serial5.read();   // ← only one byte per call
        // ... parser ...
    }
}
```

If the RPi writes the 8 bytes of the frame in a burst (which is what `pyserial` does), the Teensy needs **8 iterations** of the `loop()` to finish parsing the frame. If one of those iterations falls inside a `runTime` or `runDistance` (see issue [#63](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/63)), the frame gets stuck in the buffer until the maneuver is completed.

**Fix:**

```cpp
void serialEvent5() {
    while (Serial5.available() > 0) {     // complete drain
        int data = Serial5.read();
        // ... same parser as before ...
    }
}
```

**Impact:** vision → motor latency decreases by ~30–80 ms in the worst case. It is **the change with the highest cost-benefit ratio** in the document.

### 4.2 [P1] `reset_input_buffer()` discards valid commands

**File:** [`software/raspberry/final_rpi/Main.py:568-572`](../../software/raspberry/final_rpi/Main.py#L568-L572)

```python
while estado == 'esperando':
    frame = vs.read()
    silver_line = False
    if ser.in_waiting > 0:
        data = ser.read()
        if data == b'\xf9':
            estado = 'linea'
        ser.reset_input_buffer()   # ← clears EVERYTHING else
```

If the Teensy sent `0xF9` and then changes state and sends another byte (e.g. `0xFF` for kill switch), that second byte **is lost** in the `reset_input_buffer()`.

**Fix:** remove the `reset_input_buffer()` after the read. If it did not match, leave the byte in the buffer (it wasn't there anyway — `ser.read()` already consumed it). If it matched, the subsequent bytes are valid and must be respected.

```python
if ser.in_waiting > 0:
    data = ser.read()
    if data == b'\xf9':
        estado = 'linea'
    # NO reset_input_buffer
```

### 4.3 [P2] Fixed frame, not rate-limited by delta

**File:** [`Main.py:664-669`](../../software/raspberry/final_rpi/Main.py#L664-L669) and `:523-524`

The RPi sends a frame on EVERY iteration of the vision loop, even if `speed`, `angle`, `green_state` have not changed. It is **30 fps × 8 bytes = 240 B/s** constant — bandwidth is not a problem, but **Teensy parser CPU is**: a drain of 8 bytes every 33 ms competes with critical loops.

**Suggested fix:**
- Maintain a minimum periodic send of 10 Hz (heartbeat).
- If all fields changed <delta_threshold and 100 ms have not passed since the last send, **omit** the send.
- Result: ~12 fps of sending in steady state, full rate when there is a change.

> **Caution:** if the `serialEvent5() while` fix is made, most of the problem disappears. This point is only worth the effort if we see measurable lag after §4.1.

### 4.4 [P2] `runDistance` and `runTime` with `delay(10)` — slow polling of the kill switch

**File:** [`main.cpp:551, 575`](../../software/teensy/firmware/src/main.cpp#L551)

`delay(10)` inside the movement while limits the polling of the switch + serial to 100 Hz. For a critical control body, it should be ≥500 Hz (= no delay). It is technical debt entangled with [#59](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/59) and [#63](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/63), not worth a separate issue.

## 5. Desynchronization Issues

### 5.1 [P1] No handshake/version on startup — a reset of the Teensy desynchronizes the system

**Symptom:** if the Teensy hangs and restarts (or you turn it off and on with the Pi running), it starts in `esperando` but the Pi may be in `linea` sending frames. The Pi never receives `0xF9` (because it has already passed), the Teensy ignores `green_state` (because it did not enter `linea`). **Result: inert robot, no diagnosis.**

**Minimum fix:**
- In `setup()` of the Teensy, send `0xFA` (own sync byte) for 2 s (every 100 ms).
- In the Pi, in ANY state, if `0xFA` arrives → reset state to `esperando`.

**Complete fix:**
- Version handshake: both sides exchange version byte at boot.
- If firmware version ≠ expected version on RPi, turn on red LED and abort.

This **also nullifies problem 5.4** (RPi does not detect reset of the Teensy).

### 5.2 [P1] No sanity check of ranges in payload

**File:** [`main.cpp:386-405`](../../software/teensy/firmware/src/main.cpp#L386-L405)

```cpp
else if (serial5state == 0)
    speed = (double)data / 100 * 100; // no clamp
else if (serial5state == 1)
    steer = ((double)data - 90) / 90; // no clamp
```

If due to an RPi bug `speed = 200` arrives, the Teensy passes 200 to `steer()`, which clamps to 159 — but that clamp is invisible to the system. Worse: if `angle` arrives as 200, `steer = (200-90)/90 = 1.22`, outside the expected range [-1, 1] that `steer()` also silently clamps.

**Fix:** explicit clamp + log if out of range. Ideally, discard the frame:

```cpp
else if (serial5state == 0) {
    if (data < 0 || data > 100) { /* log + ignore */ return; }
    speed = data;
}
```

### 5.3 [P1] No CRC or checksum — silent bit flip

**Symptom:** the USB-serial cable is robust but the competition rack has a lot of noise from DC motors and servos. A bit flip in `green_state` (e.g. `7` → `5`) is **silent** — there is no detection.

**Minimum fix:** XOR of the 4 bytes of payload, attached as byte 9.

```
[0xFF, speed, 0xFE, angle, 0xFD, green, 0xFC, silver, CRC]
```

**Cost:** 1 extra byte (12 % overhead). Very cheap. Detecting simple bit flips covers ~80 % of cases.

**Complete fix:** CRC-8 polynomial 0x07. Detects more errors. Precomputed table in flash to avoid affecting performance.

### 5.4 [P1] RPi does not detect if the Teensy has restarted

Covered by §5.1 with the handshake `0xFA`.

### 5.5 [P2] Potential collision between sync bytes and payload

Currently:
- `speed` ∈ [0, 100] → does not touch [252, 255]. ✅
- `angle` ∈ [0, 180] (after `+90`) → does not touch [252, 255]. ✅
- `green_state` ∈ {0..17} → does not touch [252, 255]. ✅
- `silver_line` ∈ {0, 1} → does not touch [252, 255]. ✅

**There is no collision today**, but **there is no enforcement**. If someone adds a new `green_state = 254`, everything breaks silently. Document as a **contract** in the code (assertion in debug, clear comment).

### 5.6 [P2] Serial5 buffer can fill during blocking operations

**File:** Teensyduino default = **1 KB** for Serial5. RPi sends 8 B × 30 fps = 240 B/s. In a blocking operation of 4 s (e.g. rescue zone), **960 B** arrive. Marginal but **close to the limit**.

After the fix in §4.1, the buffer drains almost instantly and ceases to be a problem. If after that there is still an overrun, consider:

```cpp
Serial5.addMemoryForRead(buffer, 4096); // 4 KB
```

## 6. Fail-safe Gaps

| # | Gap | Risk | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | Pi hangs → Teensy continues executing last `speed`/`steer` | **Critical** — robot goes off track | Issue [#53](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/53) (heartbeat) |
| 6.2 | Teensy resets → Pi does not know | High — inert robot without diagnosis | §5.1 (handshake) |
| 6.3 | Serial cable disconnects → both sides ignore | **Critical** | §6.1 + bidirectional heartbeat |
| 6.4 | I2C sensor hangs (BNO055/APDS9960) → loop blocked | High — Pi cannot command emergency stop | Issues [#27](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/27) [#61](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/61) [#62](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/62) |
| 6.5 | RPi `ser` with `timeout=None` — `ser.read()` infinite blocking | Medium — only if someone forgets the guard `in_waiting>0` | New issue (see §9) |
| 6.6 | No frame counter/log → impossible post-mortem | Medium — blind coaching | New issue (see §9) |
| 6.7 | No "software emergency STOP" button from RPi | Medium — only the physical switch for | Discussion: see §7 phase 3 |

### 6.1 Heartbeat — concrete proposal

There is already an issue ([#53](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/53)) but without design. Proposal:

**Teensy Side:**
```cpp
elapsedMillis lastFrameMs;
const unsigned long FRAME_TIMEOUT_MS = 500;

void loop() {
    serialEvent5();  // drains
    if (lastFrameMs > FRAME_TIMEOUT_MS) {
        // No recent command → safe STOP
        speed = 0;
        steer = 0;
        digitalWrite(LED_ROJO, HIGH);  // visual diagnosis
    } else {
        digitalWrite(LED_ROJO, LOW);
    }
    // ... rest of the loop ...
}

// inside serialEvent5(), when a frame is completed:
lastFrameMs = 0;
```

**RPi Side (in main loop):**
```python
last_ack = time.monotonic()
TEENSY_TIMEOUT = 0.5   # 500 ms

# every time a byte is received from the Teensy:
last_ack = time.monotonic()

# every N frames:
if time.monotonic() - last_ack > TEENSY_TIMEOUT:
    print("[ERROR] Teensy not responding — degrading to STOP")
    output = bytes([255, 0, 254, 90, 253, 0, 252, 0])  # speed=0, angle=center
    ser.write(output)
```

## 7. Migration Plan by Phases

> **Philosophy:** first the fixes that **do not change the protocol** and reduce 80% of the risk. Only then consider protocol v2.

### Phase 1 — Minimum Fixes (≤1 week, without changing protocol)

| # | Change | Issue | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `serialEvent5()` in `while` (§4.1) | new §9.1 | 15 min | Low |
| 2 | Remove `reset_input_buffer()` post-read (§4.2) | new §9.2 | 15 min | Low |
| 3 | Heartbeat Teensy → STOP at 500 ms (§6.1) | [#53](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/53) | 1 h | Medium |
| 4 | Handshake `0xFA` at Teensy boot (§5.1) | new §9.3 | 30 min | Low |
| 5 | Clamp + flush in RPi `_send_frame()` | [#66](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/66) | 30 min | Low |
| 6 | RPi `ser` with `timeout=0.05` (§6.5) | new §9.4 | 5 min | Low |

**Expected state after Phase 1:** robot **fail-safe** against Pi crash and Teensy reset. Lower latency. No silent command loss.

### Phase 2 — Robustness (1-2 weeks)

| # | Change | Issue | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | Sanity check of ranges in Teensy parser (§5.2) | new §9.5 | 30 min |
| 8 | Logging of RX/TX frames (§6.6) | new §9.6 | 1 h |
| 9 | Drain `serialEvent5` in `runTime/runDistance/runAngle` | [#63](https://github.com/IITA-Proyectos/rcj-2026-rescue-line-iita-salta-robocup/issues/63) | 1 h |
| 10 | Document range contract in code (§5.5) | new §9.7 | 30 min |

### Phase 3 — Protocol v2 (post-world cup, optional)

Only if Phase 1 + 2 are not sufficient:

```
[ 0xAA, LEN, OPCODE, payload..., CRC8 ]
```

- `0xAA` unique sync.
- `LEN` length byte.
- `OPCODE` distinguishes message type (vision frame, ack, RPi→Teensy command, etc.).
- `payload` variable.
- `CRC8` poly 0x07.

**Pros:** robust, extensible, rich bidirectional telemetry.
**Cons:** rewrite of the parser on both sides. Regression risk. **Do not do before the world cup.**

## 10. Pre-World Cup Checklist (canonical)

When Phase 1+2 is completed, check here:

- [ ] Teensy heartbeat verified: disconnect Pi → motors stop in <600 ms.
- [ ] Teensy reset verified: turn off/on Teensy with Pi running → both return to `esperando`.
- [ ] Latency measured vision → motor < 100 ms (typical case).
- [ ] Frame loss < 0.1 % in 5 minutes of continuous operation (with telemetry).
- [ ] No warnings in `pio run` on Teensy side.
- [ ] No warnings from pyserial in `python -W all Main.py`.
- [ ] Automated tests of Teensy parser (`pio test`) running in CI.
- [ ] `testing/TEST_LOG.md` with the last 10 runs on bench/track.
